history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE -- keep-or-drop decision needed: the Chintamani Parasnath Jain Temple, also called Shri Godisa Parshwanath Bhagwan Ka Mandir, is a Jain temple dedicated to Lord Parshvanath, located on a hillock on the western outskirts of Barmer city (at the end of Sadar Road). It is famed for its magnificent sculptures, ornamental paintings and rich glass-inlay work in the interior. Rajasthan Tourism dates it to the 16th century (constructed by Shri Nemaji Jivaji Bohra), while travel sources claim the 12th century -- the conflict is flagged. This is the Barmer city Chintamani, distinct from the Chintamani Parshwanath Jain temples at Jaisalmer fort, Merta City and Surat (do not conflate). CSV town 'Barmer' is approximately correct for Barmer city; district Barmer.

name: Chintamani Parshvanath Jain Temple
town_description: Barmer, in the Thar desert of western Rajasthan, is named after its founder Bahad Rao Parmar and is known as a city of temples and traditional crafts.
